thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Pager: elevated 504s from gateway -> upstream timeouts for /v1/generate (region: us-west1). Impacting ~12% of requests, started approx 23:05 UTC. Correlation sample: cid=893f2b4a, cid=61b4f2d1.

morgan: oncall here, ack. putting folks in huddle. any active deploys?

lee: not aware of deploys in last hour. seeing a sharp rise in gateway retry loops and increased upstream connection resets in the proxy.

nina: pulling kvlogs now for the affected window (23:03-23:11). running quick grep for the cids.

lee: hypothesis1: upstream model workers saturating -> slow responses -> gateway retries amplify latency -> timeouts. hypothesis2: network blip between proxy and runtime causing connection resets.

morgan: triage plan: 1) gather sample request traces and full request/response headers 2) search for correlation ids in runtime logs 3) share gzipped log bundle to thread 4) temporary mitigation: disable retries on gateway for /v1/generate and enable route fallback to smaller model variant.

tom: Customer impact: started getting 5 customer reports. Support: adding note to status page draft.

incident-bot: created incident INC-2026-337, pager assigned to morgan. Conference bridge: +1-555-1234 ext 888.

nina: grep output snippet for cid=893f2b4a:
```
2026-03-09T23:05:12Z [request] cid=893f2b4a route=/v1/generate upstream=runtime-a-3 status=200 latency_ms=1200 kv_cache_hit=false
2026-03-09T23:05:12Z [proxy] cid=893f2b4a connection_reset by peer after 950ms
2026-03-09T23:05:13Z [gateway] cid=893f2b4a retry=1 response=504
```

morgan: interesting — runtime responded but proxy saw connection_reset. suggests unstable connection piggybacking on heavy tails.

lee: I'm seeing a spike in dial timeouts between proxy frontends and runtime nodes starting at 23:04:30, matching tail latencies. attaching ingress metric image: https://dashboards.redwood/influx/ingress-tail-23:04-23:12 (shareable).

nina: uploaded log bundle to: https://logs.redwood/internal/bundles/2367896543.tar.gz (contains kvlogs, proxy logs, runtime traces). password: redwood! (temp, rotating).

sara: adding product context — a few high-volume customers hit retries; some reported duplicated charges from client-side retried requests. flagging billing team.

morgan: immediate mitigations executed: 1) disabled gateway automatic retries for /v1/generate :white_check_mark: 2) activated fallback route to model-small for 10% of traffic :white_check_mark: 3) increased proxy connection pool soft limit by 20% on us-west1 frontends (hotfix) :white_check_mark:

lee: mitigation logs show 504 rate fell from 12% -> 3% within 90s of changes. good signal. continuing to collect samples for full RCA.

nina: pulled 50 request traces and annotated head-of-line latencies. common pattern: large request sets (seq_len>2048) push runtime token generation beyond 1s, proxy keepalive window closes when combined with other slow inflight requests. sample ids: cid=893f2b4a, cid=61b4f2d1, cid=a1c3d9b2.

morgan: action items (in-thread):
- lee: follow up on proxy keepalive/timeouts and dialer settings.
- nina: correlate runtime worker GC/CPU/IO at wall clock for the cids.
- tom: update customers + incident page with mitigations and ETA for RCA.
- sara: track billing exposure and customer escalations.

lee: quick check — found a recent config change to proxy dial_timeout from 1.2s -> 0.9s during last infra rollout (approved), which would make the system less tolerant of long tail responses. PR: https://git.redwood/infra/PR-4521.

morgan: that PR + heavy tail requests explains behavior: more connection resets because dial_timeout too short. nina, can you map that change timestamp to when the spike started?

nina: dial_timeout change merged at 22:50, rollout completed 22:58. spike starts 23:04. matches the timing after gradual rollout.

lee: hypothesis strengthened: aggressive dial timeout + heavy tail runtime requests -> more proxy resets -> gateway considers request failed -> retries -> amplification.

morgan: recommend for RCA short-term: revert dial_timeout to 1.2s on us-west1 frontends and schedule canary rollback. longer-term: autoscaling headroom and per-route timeout tuning. who can own the rollback?

lee: I can own rollback, will coordinate with eng-infra and schedule canary steps. will post progress.

incident-bot: rollback job queued: job-7783 (revert dial_timeout) — ETA 10m.

lee: rollback started at 23:22. monitoring.

morgan: monitoring shows 504s drop to 0.8% after rollback. good. hold for 30m to confirm.

tom: status page updated: "Partial service disruption for text generation resolved; mitigation in place. Full RCA to follow."

sara: capturing customer impact notes for follow-up call tomorrow.

nina: additional artifact: sample runtime trace with long tail attached:
```
trace_id=a1c3d9b2
span[0]: accept_request (10ms)
span[1]: model_load_shard (1ms)
span[2]: generate_tokens (1100ms)
span[3]: stream_flush (200ms)
```

morgan: closing loop: mitigation successful, rollback confirmed. leaving thread open for RCA write-up — assign to nina+lee to draft timeline and hypothesis section. I'll convert INC-2026-337 to postmortem flag and assign owners. :mag: 

lee: will include timeline, log excerpts (cid samples), config diff (PR-4521), rollback steps, and suggested guardrails (canary speed limits, per-route retry gating).

nina: will produce annotated KV log samples and runtime CPU/IO graphs. planning to include recommended quantization/batching suggestions to reduce tail latencies for long sequences.

tom: noting billing follow-up with finance on duplicated billing window for customers impacted.

incident-bot: incident updated: mitigated=true, next_step=RCA_draft_assigned, severity=sev2.
